title: $108m super rip-off for teenage workers
full_text:
About 124,000 working Queensland teens will miss out on a combined $108m in super this financial year, new analysis shows.
Because under-18s don’t get the 12 per cent super guarantee unless they work more than 30 hours a week in one job, the Super Members Council estimates the average Queensland teenager will miss out on $870.
Chief executive Misha Schubert said young women were more likely to be affected by the exclusion than men – a gap that continues throughout working lives – missing out on around $2500 in super contributions before they turn 18.
By retirement age that grows to around $11,200.
“A young person who earns a wage should also be paid super. Yet this outdated and discriminatory law treats teen workers differently just because of their age and their hours,” she said.
“Many teenagers have their first jobs in retail, hospitality, care and community services. These are real jobs, with real wages, and they should come with real super.
“The earliest super contributions matter because they have the longest time to compound. Missing out on hundreds of dollars as a teenager can mean missing out on thousands by retirement.” The council wants the exclusion to be abolished after a “sensible” transition period.
A push to reform the law is being led by the Greens, with a Senate inquiry due to report to parliament in November. In July, Labor members at the party’s triennial national conference committed the ALP to compulsory superannuation for teenagers.
